whatIs.title: What Is Steganography?
whatIs.description: Steganography is the practice of hiding information inside digital media such as images without visibly changing the original file. Unlike encryption, which makes data unreadable, steganography makes data undetectable.

vs.title: Steganography vs Encryption
vs.subtitle: Understanding the difference between hiding data and protecting it.
vs.tip: Security Pro-Tip: For maximum security, always encrypt your sensitive message first, then use steganography to hide the resulting ciphertext inside an image. This provides both concealment and data protection.

forensics.title: Detecting Hidden Data
forensics.description: While LSB steganography is visually undetectable, advanced forensic tools can detect patterns in the least significant bits. Professionals use techniques like Chi-square analysis and Visual Attacks to find hidden payloads.

items.title: Statistical Analysis
items.desc: Detecting deviations in bit distribution that indicate non-natural data.

items.title: Visual Attacks
items.desc: Isolating bit planes to reveal structural anomalies in the noise.

items.title: Histogram Shifts
items.desc: Identifying subtle shifts in color frequencies caused by bit mutation.

items.d: Images with lots of texture and detail (like nature shots) are better carriers than flat, solid colors where bit mutations are easier to spot statistically.
Always encrypt your text with AES-256 before hiding it. This ensures that even if the steganography is detected, the data remains unreadable.
Resizing or re-compressing an encoded image will almost certainly destroy the hidden data. Always share the original output file.

notice.title: Steganography Is Not Encryption
notice.description: Steganography relies on obscurity, not computational hardness. While it hides the existence of a message, it does not necessarily protect the content if the steganography is detected.
points: Always combine with strong encryption (AES-256) for sensitive data.
Use lossless formats (PNG) to avoid data corruption.
Never use for illegal or unethical concealment.
Be aware that forensic tools can detect LSB mutations.
